messages.author: c1c3dbde7a2d806d
messages.subject: Hierarchical Factor Model
parts:
Hi Phil,

With the key words "hierarchical" or "second order" I was not able to find a post in this forum, so I hope I am not duplicating stuff that is already here...

I was wondering whether it is possible to estimate a second order factor model with mirt? What I mean is this:

F1 = 1-10
F2 = 11-20
F3 = 21-30

And instead of correlating these three factors a higher order factor should be defined, mimicking it here in your language:
G = F1, F2, F3

Please don't ask why. It is a reviewer's request I have not been able to fend off through reasoning with her/him.

Very sorry if I did not find this in your detailed documentation or slides on the web!
jan

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Hierarchical Factor Model
parts:
Hi Jan,

No unfortunately mirt doesn't support hierarchical models (yet). I've thought about how to include them with the MH-RM algorithm since it seems flexible enough to do, but haven't found the time to write it out yet. I'll keep you posted/add it to the NEWS when I do get around to it, but the answer right now is no. 

There was some software written by Yanyan Sheng a while back which can estimate these models using a pure Bayesian framework though, so that might be worth exploring if the reviewer really insists (though in my opinion the bifactor model is almost always the better modeling choice compared to hierarchical approaches). Cheers.

Phil
